Description: Primary strategy used to correct for instrumental isotopic mass fractionation. In solution MC-ICP-MS, instrumental mass bias is typically 3–5%/amu and must be corrected before isotope ratios can be interpreted geochemically. Four main strategies: (1) Sample-standard bracketing (SSB): alternating sample and isotopic standard measurements; bias interpolated linearly between bracketing measurements. (2) Double-spike: a mixture of two enriched isotopes of the analyte element added before digestion provides an internal monitor of both instrumental and chemical mass fractionation. (3) Internal normalization: an element of known isotopic composition added to samples and standards; measured ratio of normalizing element used to calculate the mass bias factor applied to analyte ratios. (4) SSB + internal normalization: both strategies applied simultaneously for redundant bias correction.

Example / Allowed Content: Monitor mass correction: 202Hg signal × (204Hg/202Hg)natural to correct 204Pb | Abundance sensitivity tailing factor measured weekly from pure U standard | None | N/A | Other: specify
Hopp+etal2021 | Neptune (Plus spec) | Un: Simultaneous monitoring of 53Cr and 60Ni on 10^12 Ω amplifiers; argides resolved by measuring on the flat-topped peak shoulder in MR or HR mode
Hu+etal2022 | Neptune Plus | Univ Chicag: Subconfiguration scaling — 166Er measured only in the subconfiguration, 163Dy in both; the 166Er/163Dy ratio is scaled onto the main configuration and multiplied by 162Er/166Er and 164Er/166Er to subtract the interferences
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: A doping calibration: "Offset δ94/90ZrNIST = −63.4 · x" where x is the total Mo/Zr atomic ratio; the reported data are uncorrected for residual Mo
Nie+Dauphas2019 | Neptune | Univ Chicago: Correction assuming a constant terrestrial 87Sr/88Sr = 0.085, with a sensitivity test over 0.0835–0.0885 showing a maximum shift of 0.008 permil
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: Monitor isotopes 184W, 186W and 187Re; abundance sensitivity determined by scanning the low mass tail of a 30 V 192Os beam using the SEM and fitting a curve to the tail — 0.5 to 1 ppm in the Os mass range
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: Online W and Re correction; abundance sensitivity greater than 1 ppm "since the analyser pressure was higher at ~2 x 10^-8 mbar"
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Mo and Ru corrections calculated from the signals on mass 95, 99 and 101, with an initial Mo correction using a mass bias relative to 91Zr/90Zr = 0.21798

Description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions, and where applicable isotope ratios, from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements. For double-spike procedures the ratios and concentrations are co-determined through the spike inversion; for conventional isotope dilution the IUPAC ID equations are used. Record 'None' where neither isotope dilution nor double-spike methods are applied.
Example / Allowed Content: Double-spike inversion (isotope ratios and concentrations co-determined) | IUPAC isotope dilution equations (concentration from separate ID spike) | None | N/A | Other: specify
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: Double-spike inversion, Rmeas = [p·RSpike + (1−p)·RStd·(Mx/Mn)^α]·(Mx/Mi)^β, solved by weighted minimisation over four ratios

Description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.
Example / Allowed Content: Extended acid rinse between samples; first measurement excluded if preceded by high-signal sample | Blank measurement inspected before each sample; session halted if blank > 0.5% of sample signal | None required for this analyte suite | N/A | None
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: On-peak-zero acid blank before each sample "to account for blank contribution as well as any 'memory' effects from the Aridus II sample introduction system during the run"
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: Desolvating nebulisers deliberately avoided because of "severe memory problems for Os"; ESI PFA-50 low-uptake nebuliser and GE Cinnabar micro-cyclonic spray chamber chosen "in the hope these would reduce the long Os washout times and poor memory usually associated with solution introduction of Os"; wash acid aspirated until the 192Os beam fell to background — a 99.99% decrease reached after 220 s for DTM
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: TD 3 mol/l HCl aspirated between analyses until the Os beam decreased to acceptable background levels

Description: The convention at which reported uncertainties are quoted — 1-sigma, 2-sigma, or a 95% confidence interval — and whether a measured spread is reported as a standard error or a standard deviation. State the convention applying to all values reported under this procedure, and state each separately where different reported quantities use different conventions. Distinct from Uncertainty Propagation Method, which addresses how component uncertainties are combined rather than how the result is quoted.
Example / Allowed Content: 2σ (95% confidence) | 1σ (68% confidence) | 95% confidence interval | 2 standard errors (2SE) | 1 standard deviation (1SD) | N/A | None
Purpose: A reported uncertainty is not interpretable without it: the same numeric value means different things at 1-sigma and at 95% confidence.
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: 2 s.d. for external reproducibility (n = 24 for Mo, n = 14 for Ba)
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: "external reproducibility is reported at the 2σ error level"; long-term reproducibility "typically 0.20‰ and 0.45‰ (2σ) for solution and laser"
Hu+etal2022 | Neptune Plus | Univ Chicag: Not stated in the section read
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: "the external reproducibility (at 2σ) of the spiked ZrNIST measurements from each run, which in all cases was similar in magnitude or slightly larger than the internal uncertainty determined from counting statistics"
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: 2SD for short- and long-term reproducibility; within-run errors as "2 standard errors of the mean (2SE = 2SD/n^0.5; where n = 45 for the Neptune analyses"
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: 2SD and 2SE, with n = 50 for the Nu Plasma analyses
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: "the 2 standard error (2se) is reported unless stated otherwise"; for samples analysed fewer than 3 times, "the largest 2 se reported for a sample analyzed multiple times has been used"
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Both quoted: "external precision expressed as 2 standard deviations (2SD)" and 2SE per analysis
vanKooten+etal2026 | Thermo Neoma | Univ: "the mean and 2 x standard error (SE) of ten individual standard-bracketed sample analyses"
Broussard+etal2026 | Neptune Plus | WUST: Stated as ± values on δ41K without an explicit convention in the section read

Description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.
Example / Allowed Content: 2σ of bracketing standard reproducibility propagated to sample | Monte Carlo simulation through double-spike inversion | ISO GUM quadrature propagation | N/A | None | Other: specify
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: External reproducibility of the spiked ZrNIST measurements from each run adopted per determination, compared against internal counting-statistics uncertainty

Description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: Spike isotope decay correction applied | Age correction for U-series disequilibrium | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: An externally-calibrated factor that converts the measured quantity into the reported quantity, how it was determined, and its uncertainty. Applies where the conversion depends on a factor calibrated against a reference of independently known value, rather than on the instrument response alone. Distinct from the fields that name the calibration material and that state which approach applies to which analyte, where the technique has them: this field records the resulting factor itself.

The measured level of the analytical blank in the session, and — where the reported quantity is a ratio — its composition, since a blank subtracted from a ratio biases the result unless its own composition is known. Companion to the blank correction method.
Purpose: Follows the criterion-versus-measurement split the library applies wherever a procedure sets a threshold and an analysis reports a value against it.
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: "Total procedural blanks were between 0.7 and 1.2 ng and thus negligible, given that several hundred ng of Mo were analyzed for each sample"
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: "The procedural blank, resulting from chemical processing and purification is ~0.05% (~0.25 µg per 500 µg S used for column chemistry)"
Hopp+etal2021 | Neptune (Plus spec) | Un: "the total procedural blank is ~70 ng and thus negligible considering that 1-2 mg Fe was purified for each sample"
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: "The total mass of non-radiogenic Pb measured in our FC-1 zircon and baddeleyite fractions is indistinguishable from the range of Pb determined in total procedural blanks"
Nie+Dauphas2019 | Neptune | Univ Chicago: "The Rb blank of the procedure (digestion and column chemistry) is ~0.14 ng, which accounts for less than 0.5% of total Rb from a typical sample (40 ng)"
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: "Total procedural blanks prepared together with Tarda and Tagish Lake contained 0.08 and 0.24 ng Zr, while total blanks treated alongside Ivuna were 0.09 and 0.13 ng Zr"
Barnes+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | ETH Zur: "The total procedural blank for Ti was 3.7 ng, resulting in a maximum blank contribution of 0.18% for Ti"

Description: The rules determining which individual analyses contribute to a reported aggregate result, together with the outcome of applying them: how many analyses were acquired, how many were included, and on what grounds any were excluded. Distinct from within-analysis outlier filtering, which removes anomalous points inside a single analysis: this field decides which whole analyses enter the reported value.
Purpose: Criteria and outcome are combined in one field because neither is interpretable without the other, following the precision/accuracy precedent.
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: Partially — "For samples analyzed several times, reported values represent the mean of pooled solution replicates". No acceptance or rejection rule stated
Hu+etal2022 | Neptune Plus | Univ Chicag: Partially — "On average, LREEs were measured nine times"; replicate matrix cuts were measured but "are not used, however, for data interpretation to avoid unnecessary influence of stable isotopic fractionation potentially induced by Mo chemistry" — an explicit exclusion, on chemical rather than statistical grounds
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: Partially — Table 1 records "Number of times the same purified Zr solution was measured independently in the MC-ICP-MS" and "Reported values are weighted means of all replicate" analyses. No rejection rule stated
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: Partially — n = 45 per analysis. No rejection rule stated
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: Partially — n = 50 per analysis. No rejection rule stated
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: "any ratio outside 2σ was discarded" — an explicit rejection rule, applied within a measurement. Reported values are "averages of repeated measurements of each sample when multiple analyses were possible"
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Partially — n stated per reference material (n = 13–99 for terrestrial RMs over 10 months; n = 17–38 for eucrites and Colony; n = 32 and n = 37 for standard sessions). No rejection rule stated
vanKooten+etal2026 | Thermo Neoma | Univ: Partially — "the mean ... of ten individual standard-bracketed sample analyses"; "Samples were typically analysed two to four times". No rejection rule stated
Broussard+etal2026 | Neptune Plus | WUST: Partially — "Each sample was measured approximately 20 times". No rejection rule stated

Description: The correlation coefficient between pairs of reported quantities whose uncertainties are not independent, together with the pair it applies to and how it was obtained. Concordia and isochron regressions cannot be reconstructed without it.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'rho(206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U) = 0.83, from the data reduction software error propagation' | 'rho = 0.31 (double-spike inversion covariance)'

Description: Physical constants and reference values used in data reduction to calculate the final reported quantity (e.g., decay constants for age calculation, standard isotope ratios, or other citable reference values used in a correction or calculation), together with their source. Distinct from the Group 6 reference-material fields, which document accepted values for specific calibration/validation materials rather than universal physical constants. Record "None" if no citable, revisable physical constants feed into this procedure's data reduction.
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: 98Mo/96Mo = 1.453173 for internal normalization; 134Ba/136Ba = 0.3078 (Carlson et al. 2007) for the TIMS half
Hopp+etal2021 | Neptune (Plus spec) | Un: 57Fe/56Fe = 0.023095 and 57Fe/54Fe = 0.362549, "the certified ratios of IRMM-014" (Craddock and Dauphas, 2010)
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: 238U/235U = 137.818 (45), 18O/16O = 0.00205 (44), and α = 0.18 ± 0.02%/amu from repeat NBS-981 analyses; U decay constants of (47); Th/U[magma] = 2.8 ± 1.0 for the initial 230Th disequilibrium correction
Nie+Dauphas2019 | Neptune | Univ Chicago: 87Sr/88Sr = 0.085, "which is the terrestrial Sr ratio", used for the 87Sr interference correction; sensitivity tested at 0.0835 and 0.0885

Description: Name and reference material identifier of the primary reference material(s) against which the instrument is calibrated — converting raw signal intensities to concentrations, or anchoring an isotope ratio as the bracketing standard or zero-delta reference. Give the material name, its source or supplier, and a citation for the accepted values used, since results calibrated against different published values for the same material are not directly comparable.
Example / Allowed Content: IRMM-014 (Fe isotopes; Taylor et al. 1992) | CRM-112a / SRM-960 (U isotopes) | NIST SRM 981 (Pb isotopes) | JMC Lyon Zn standard | NIST SRM 3102a (Sb) | In-house single-element standard solution: specify | N/A | None | Other: specify
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: In-house S_Alfa and S_Spex 20 ppm S solutions, calibrated against IAEA-S-1, S-2, S-4 and NBS-123
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: UMd, DTM, LOsST and DROsS Os reference materials
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: NIST SRM984 RbCl; BCR-2 as an alternative bracketing standard in some sessions

Description: How often the primary calibration or bracketing standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session. Specify the bracketing scheme where a fixed one is used, such as one standard measurement before and after each sample.
Example / Allowed Content: SSB: one standard before and one after every sample | One standard every 3 samples | Start and end of session only | N/A | None | Other: specify
Hu+etal2022 | Neptune Plus | Univ Chicag: Every sample, spaced by 300 s rinsing
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: Every sample — "Each sample measurement was individually bracketed"
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: Every sample (bracketing), plus an external pure Rb solution "during each analytical session"
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Each session — "The Zr standard material NIST SRM 3169 was analyzed in each session"

Description: Quality-control reference material(s) measured as unknowns alongside samples to assess accuracy independently and to monitor drift. Give the material name, its source, and a citation for the accepted or reference values used for comparison.
Example / Allowed Content: BHVO-2 (Fe isotopes; Dauphas & Rouxel 2006 compilation) | BCR-2 | NIST SRM 960 or equivalent U standard | NIST SRM 981 (Pb) | AGV-2 | N/A | None | Other: specify
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: BHVO-2, "several digestions of which were processed through the full analytical protocol and analyzed together with each set of samples"
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: Sch-M-2 anhydrite mineral standard; geological reference samples with known isotope compositions
Nie+Dauphas2019 | Neptune | Univ Chicago: BHVO-2, BCR-2, BE-N, W-2, AGV-2, GSR-1, GS-N, G-A, G-3; DTS-2b and PCC-1 synthetic mixes; Allende
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: BCR-2, AGV-2, BHVO-2, GS-N and other terrestrial rocks
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: BHVO-2, BCR-2, AGV-1, SCo-1; eucrites Bouvante and Bereba; CO chondrite Colony
vanKooten+etal2026 | Thermo Neoma | Univ: BHVO2 and DTS-2b, "processed alongside the samples"

Description: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the analyte together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '2SE predicted from counting statistics over 45 cycles' | '~0.6% (1 sigma), counting statistics plus propagated uncertainties' | 'N/A'
Keyed By: sample > sampling unit x reported property
Purpose: Where a procedure reports both, agreement indicates the measurement is shot-noise limited, and a larger observed scatter indicates a further source of variance.
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: Internal uncertainty determined from counting statistics, used as the comparison against the external reproducibility adopted per determination; value not tabulated

Metadata Item: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of a single measurement, derived from the scatter of the cycles, sweeps or integrations that make it up, together with the method used to assess it. State the statistic (2SE, 2SD, 1s RSD), the number of cycles it is computed over, and the reported quantity it applies to. Distinct from Counting Statistics Error, which records the uncertainty predicted from the counts rather than the scatter observed; where a procedure reports both, record the observed value here and the predicted value there.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '2SE = 2SD/sqrt(n), n = 45 cycles' | '+/-0.001-0.002 (2SE) on 206Pb/204Pb' | '~2.6% (2SE) on single-spot ages' | 'N/A'
Keyed By: sample > sampling unit x reported property
Purpose: This is the finest of the three precision levels the library records, below within-session and between-session precision: it describes the repeatability of one analysis rather than agreement between analyses, and is normally the smallest of the three.
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: Internal uncertainty determined from counting statistics; stated to be similar in magnitude to or slightly smaller than the external reproducibility adopted per determination
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: Within-run errors for individual analyses quoted as 2 standard errors of the mean, 2SE = 2SD/n^0.5, with n = 45 cycles
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: Within-run errors for individual analyses quoted as 2 standard errors of the mean, 2SE = 2SD/n^0.5, with n = 50 cycles

Metadata Item: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of repeated measurements within a single analytical session and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values. The assessment method must specify the reference material or standard measured, the number of replicates n, and the statistic reported (1s RSD, 2s RSD, 2SD, 2SE, 95% CI). Distinct from the internal precision of a single measurement, which derives from counting statistics over the cycles of that measurement rather than from repeated analyses.
Example / Allowed Content: 2SD = 0.03‰ on δ56Fe (n=10 BHVO-2); session | 2σ = 0.004‰ on δ238U (n=9 CRM-112a brackets) | N/A | None | Other: specify
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: External reproducibility at 2 sigma of the spiked ZrNIST measurements from each run, adopted as the uncertainty on each determination and stated to be similar to or slightly larger than the internal counting-statistics uncertainty
Nowell+etal2008 | Neptune | Durham AHIGL: Short-term reproducibility of standards analysed in a single analytical session, quoted as 2 standard deviations (2SD). Distinct from the within-run internal error, which the paper quotes separately as 2SE of the mean, 2SE = 2SD/n^0.5 with n = 45 for the Neptune and n = 50 for the Nu Plasma analyses
Nowell+etal2008 | Nu Plasma | NIGL: Short-term reproducibility of standards analysed in a single analytical session, quoted as 2 standard deviations (2SD). Distinct from the within-run internal error, which the paper quotes separately as 2SE of the mean, 2SE = 2SD/n^0.5 with n = 45 for the Neptune and n = 50 for the Nu Plasma analyses

Metadata Item: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months — long-term or intermediate precision — and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values, specifying the reference material, the number of measurements and sessions, the time span covered, and the statistic reported.
Example / Allowed Content: 2SD = 0.030‰ on δ56Fe (n=23 sessions; BHVO-1; Dauphas et al. 2009) | 2SD = 0.005‰ on δ238U (n > 50 analyses; CRM-112a) | N/A | None | Other: specify
Purpose: Long-term precision is normally poorer than within-session precision and is the figure a data user should carry when comparing results from different sessions.
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: External reproducibility from repeated BHVO-2 measurements: ±0.14 for ε97Mo to ±0.39 for ε92Mo (2 s.d., n = 24); Ba ±0.13 for ε135Ba to ±0.31 for ε138Ba (2 s.d., n = 14)
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: "Long-term reproducibility of S isotope compositions is typically 0.20‰ and 0.45‰ (2σ) for solution and laser"; long-term reproducibility of in-house solution standards within ±0.2‰
IbanezMejia+Tissot2020 | Nu Plasma II |: External reproducibility at 2σ of the spiked ZrNIST measurements from each run
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: "the long-term reproducibility was ±0.01‰ (n = 40)" from a pure Rb ICP-MS solution run as an external standard each session
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Terrestrial RMs measured over 10 months (n = 13–99) give average 2SD of 0.3, 0.2 and 1.0 for ε91Zr, ε92Zr and ε96Zr; "The external precision estimated from the geological sample measurements integrates the uncertainty introduced by the chemical separation procedure and mass spectrometry"

Description: Offset between measured and accepted values for secondary reference materials, and the method used to assess it. Specify the reference material and the source of its accepted values, the number of analyses, and the quantities assessed. Report systematic biases and their likely causes. Express the offset in the form appropriate to what the procedure reports - percent relative bias for concentrations, or deviation in delta or ratio units for isotopic quantities.
Example / Allowed Content: % deviation from published δ56Fe for BHVO-1 compilation value | Agreement with certified δ238U of IRMM-3636 spike solution | Z-score relative to interlaboratory consensus | N/A | None | Other: specify
Budde+etal2016 | Neptune Plus | IfP Müns: "The εiMo values obtained for BHVO-2 are indistinguishable from the Alfa Aesar standard, demonstrating that the Mo isotopic data are accurate"
Craddock+etal2008 | Thermo NEPTUNE | WHO: Assessed against IAEA and NBS reference materials on the V-CDT scale and against geological reference samples with known compositions
Hu+etal2022 | Neptune Plus | Univ Chicag: Assessed in a dedicated "Assessment of data accuracy" section, using replicate matrix cuts and a processed geostandard
Nie+Dauphas2019 | Neptune | Univ Chicago: NIST SRM984 treated as a sample, plus synthetic DTS-2b+SRM984 and PCC-1+SRM984 mixes, "gave δ87Rb values of zero within error"; geostandards and Allende "yielded reproducible results that agree with literature data"
Pringle+Moynier2017 | Neptune Plus | IPG: An aliquot of SRM984 passed through the full chemistry gave δ87Rb = 0.00 ± 0.03‰, "confirming that no isotope fractionation is caused by the Rb purification procedure"; Allende duplicate splits agreed at 0.12 ± 0.02‰ and 0.14 ± 0.04‰
Schönbächler+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | E: Terrestrial and meteorite reference materials measured repeatedly to verify data quality; doping tests with Ti, V, Cr, Mo, Hf and W showed "the observed trace levels have no effect on the accuracy of the Zr isotope data"
vanKooten+etal2026 | Thermo Neoma | Univ: BHVO2 and DTS-2b processed alongside the samples
Broussard+etal2026 | Neptune Plus | WUST: "The average d41K value for BHVO-2 was −0.448 ± 0.027‰ which is within error of its previously reported values, for example, −0.46 ± 0.09‰ (Wang et al., 2021)"
Barnes+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | WUSTL: "To monitor data quality, the geostandard BHVO-2 was analysed alongside all sample analyses"
Barnes+etal2025 | Neptune Plus | ETH Zur: Reproducibility verified against measurements made "under conditions similar to the methods used", quoted as ±0.16 and ±0.26 ε50Ti (2 s.d.)

Description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per analyte, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.
Formula or approach used to calculate the detection limits, with a citation for the method where one exists. Must be consistent with the values reported in Detection Limit.
Example / Allowed Content: 3σ blank | 3σ background | 3σ counting statistics | 3× blank mean | Poisson statistics | N/A | None

Description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Mandatory at analysis level when concentrations near the LOD are reported.
Example / Allowed Content: 10σ blank | 10σ background | 10× LOD | 3.3× LOD | S/N ≥ 10 | N/A | None

Description: The statistic reported to show whether scatter among the contributing analyses exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts, together with its value. The procedure may still state an acceptance threshold, which belongs with the inclusion criteria.
Purpose: Answers whether a reported aggregate is defensible as a single population. The value cannot be known before the analysis.

Description: Any procedure- or analysis-specific information not captured by a structured field anywhere in this TAPP — including anomalies, deviations from the registered procedure, instrument modifications, and supplementary context. Scope is the whole document, not Group 6: this is the last field of the TAPP and covers all six groups. Use sparingly; a structured field is preferred for anything that can be formally categorised.
